user_request: AI document intelligence platform using AWS, OCR, secure storage, RAG, authentication and APIs.
normalized_request: Build an AI-powered document intelligence platform that ingests documents via OCR, stores them securely, enables semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and exposes capabilities through authenticated REST APIs.

requirements.description: Ingest documents from multiple sources and extract text content using OCR
Store documents securely with encryption at rest and in transit
Index documents for semantic search and retrieval using embeddings
Enable RAG to generate AI-powered answers by combining LLM inference with retrieved documents
Provide REST API endpoints for document upload, search, and query operations
Authenticate and authorize API requests with role-based access control
Monitor system health, API usage, and application performance

components.name: DOCUMENT_OCR_ENGINE
components.description: Extract text and metadata from scanned documents, PDFs, and images using optical character recognition

components.name: SECURE_DOCUMENT_STORAGE
components.description: Store ingested documents with encryption at rest, access controls, and audit logging

components.name: SEMANTIC_SEARCH_AND_RAG
components.description: Generate embeddings for documents, index them in a vector store, retrieve relevant documents, and orchestrate RAG queries with LLM inference to produce AI-generated answers

components.name: REST_API_SERVER
components.description: Expose document upload, search, and query operations through authenticated HTTP endpoints

components.name: API_AUTHENTICATION_AND_AUTHORIZATION
components.description: Implement token-based authentication, session management, and role-based access control for API endpoints

components.name: TRANSPORT_ENCRYPTION
components.description: Enforce TLS/SSL for all API and service-to-service communication

components.name: OBSERVABILITY_AND_MONITORING
components.description: Log API requests, track system metrics, monitor application performance, and generate audit trails

components.name: AWS_CLOUD_INTEGRATION
components.description: Coordinate deployment and integration with AWS services for compute, storage, and managed AI capabilities

decisions.reason: FortifyAuth-API is the strongest candidate for COMP-005, scoring 87 in evaluation. It directly implements all core component requirements: token-based authentication (JWT), role-based access control (RBAC), and session management with refresh token rotation. The tech stack (Node.js, Express, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Redis) is well-established for production API security. Recent maintenance (2026-07-01) indicates active development. CAND-020 (maintainerd-auth, score 86) and CAND-019 (ErtisAuth, score 83) are strong alternatives with similar capability scores, but FortifyAuth's explicit feature list (JWT, RBAC, refresh tokens, 2FA, API keys, audit logs) provides more concrete evidence. REUSE is appropriate because FortifyAuth appears to be a standalone authentication service requiring only configuration and integration with the REST API gateway, not substantial customization.

While CAND-015 (fess, score 76) provides REST API capabilities and multi-source document ingestion, available candidates are insufficient for a complete REST_API_SERVER component tailored to the enterprise document AI requirements. CAND-015 is a search backend providing query endpoints but lacks explicit support for document upload operations, RAG query orchestration, and deep integration with the broader system (OCR ingestion, semantic indexing, authentication). CAND-016 (node-fhir-server-core, score 58) is domain-specific to healthcare. CAND-017 (cornflow, score 50) is an optimization server unrelated to document operations. None of the candidates provide evidence of comprehensive REST API design for all three operations required: document upload (REQ-001 support), semantic search (REQ-003 support), and RAG query (REQ-004 support). A custom REST API server in Node.js/Express or Python/FastAPI is necessary to orchestrate the complete workflow, integrate with Haystack (COMP-003), Mayan EDMS (COMP-002), FortifyAuth (COMP-005), and observability platform (COMP-007). BUILD allows architectural flexibility and ensures all integration points are properly designed.

Haystack is the strongest candidate for COMP-003, scoring 79 in evaluation. It is explicitly described as an AI orchestration framework with direct support for RAG, semantic search, embeddings, retrieval pipelines, and modular agent workflows. The framework provides explicit control over retrieval, routing, and generation—core requirements for orchestrating RAG queries with LLM inference (REQ-004). Recent maintenance (2026-08-29) indicates active development. CAND-011 (fess, score 67) and CAND-012 (semantic-ai, score 70) are viable alternatives but fess is a search backend rather than orchestration framework, and semantic-ai has older maintenance history. Haystack's architectural focus on orchestration and modularity makes it suitable for REUSE with minimal customization for connecting to specific vector stores, LLM providers, and document retrieval sources.

No candidate adequately addresses COMP-008 requirements for coordinating deployment and integration with AWS services for the enterprise Document AI platform. Available candidates address only narrow AWS aspects: CAND-030 (aws-iot-reference-architecture, score 42) focuses on IoT provisioning; CAND-031 (CloudWatchX, score 42) addresses monitoring only; CAND-032 (iot-framework, score 32) targets microcontroller connectivity; CAND-033 (cloud-ops-toolkit, score 51) provides operational scripts; CAND-034 (Polly-Rust-Server, score 44) integrates TTS service. None address the comprehensive requirements: deploying containerized services (OCR engine, REST API, embedding service, LLM inference), provisioning storage (Mayan EDMS, vector database, document bucket), configuring networking (VPC, security groups, load balancing), managing authentication/secrets, and orchestrating inter-service communication. COMP-008 is best addressed through a custom deployment architecture (IaC with Terraform/CloudFormation) that orchestrates AWS services (EC2/ECS for compute, S3 for storage, RDS for databases, VPC for networking, Secrets Manager for credentials) and integrates third-party components (Haystack, Mayan EDMS, OpenObserve). This ensures architectural alignment with the complete system.

GdoczAI directly addresses document OCR requirements with explicit multi-engine OCR capability for PDFs and images, producing structured JSON output for metadata extraction. It is the strongest candidate for COMP-001, scoring 80 in the evaluation. While CAND-002 (Doliphin-OCR, score 75) and CAND-003 (open-semantic-search, score 74) are viable alternatives, GdoczAI's explicit focus on structured output and recent maintenance (2026-08-26) make it the preferred choice. However, confidence is moderate (72) because critical evidence is missing: no license type disclosed, no security audit information, no GitHub statistics, no performance benchmarks, and no evidence of enterprise adoption. data_flow: User uploads document via REST API (COMP-004) POST /documents/upload endpoint → Request authenticated via FortifyAuth-API (COMP-005) JWT validation → Document routed to GdoczAI (COMP-001) OCR engine

GdoczAI (COMP-001) extracts text, metadata, and confidence scores → Outputs structured JSON → Stored in Mayan EDMS (COMP-002) with encryption at rest (COMP-006 TLS for transit) → Access logged to OpenObserve (COMP-007)

Extracted text forwarded to Haystack (COMP-003) embedding service → Embedding model generates dense vectors → Vectors indexed in managed vector database (COMP-008) → Original document chunks stored for retrieval

User submits semantic search query via REST API (COMP-004) GET /documents/search → Authenticated via FortifyAuth-API (COMP-005) → Query string embedded by Haystack (COMP-003) → Vector similarity search executed → Relevant documents retrieved from Mayan EDMS (COMP-002)

User submits RAG query via REST API (COMP-004) POST /documents/query → Authenticated and authorized via FortifyAuth-API (COMP-005) RBAC → Query embedded by Haystack (COMP-003) → Semantic search retrieves top-K relevant document chunks → Chunks formatted with user query and sent to LLM (via AWS Bedrock or external provider, coordinated by COMP-008) → LLM generates grounded answer → Response returned to user via REST API

All API requests logged with user ID, endpoint, method, status code, latency → Logs streamed to OpenObserve (COMP-007) over TLS/SSL (COMP-006) → Dashboards display request throughput, error rates, authentication events
OCR processing metrics (documents processed, confidence scores, processing time) → Forwarded to OpenObserve (COMP-007) → Alerts triggered on quality degradation or processing latency spikes
Document access events (read, write, delete operations) audited by Mayan EDMS (COMP-002) → Audit trails exported to OpenObserve (COMP-007) for compliance tracking
Haystack (COMP-003) RAG pipeline metrics: retrieval latency, LLM response time, token usage → Metrics exported to OpenObserve (COMP-007) for performance monitoring

implementation_phases.name: Foundation and Security Infrastructure
activities: Set up AWS account, VPC, subnets, and security groups (COMP-008)
Provision RDS PostgreSQL instances for Mayan EDMS and FortifyAuth-API (COMP-008, COMP-002, COMP-005)
Deploy FortifyAuth-API with user store and session management (COMP-005); configure JWT signing keys; provision Redis cache for session store
Implement TLS/SSL certificate provisioning and renewal via AWS Certificate Manager (COMP-006); configure cipher suites (TLS 1.2+, strong ciphers)
Deploy OpenObserve for centralized logging and monitoring (COMP-007); configure log collectors for all services
Set up AWS Secrets Manager for storing database credentials, API keys, and sensitive configuration
Configure CI/CD pipeline for automated container builds and deployment

implementation_phases.name: Data Storage and Management Layer
activities: Deploy Mayan EDMS with encryption-at-rest configuration (AES-256) (COMP-002)
Integrate Mayan EDMS with FortifyAuth-API for RBAC and access control (COMP-005, COMP-002)
Configure S3 buckets for document staging and temporary OCR processing artifacts (COMP-008)
Provision managed vector database (Amazon OpenSearch Service, Weaviate, or Milvus) for embeddings storage (COMP-008, COMP-003)
Implement database backup and disaster recovery procedures for Mayan EDMS and vector DB
Configure audit logging in Mayan EDMS to export events to OpenObserve (COMP-007)

implementation_phases.name: OCR and Ingestion Pipeline
activities: Containerize GdoczAI OCR engine; configure multi-engine OCR for PDFs and images (COMP-001)
Deploy GdoczAI on ECS with auto-scaling based on document queue depth (COMP-008)
Implement document ingestion workflow: file upload → queuing → OCR processing → metadata extraction → storage in Mayan EDMS
Set up S3 event triggers to invoke OCR pipeline on document uploads (COMP-008)
Implement error handling and retry logic for failed OCR jobs; export metrics to OpenObserve (COMP-007)
Configure OCR confidence score monitoring; alert on quality degradation

implementation_phases.name: Semantic Search and RAG Orchestration
activities: Deploy Haystack framework on ECS (COMP-003); configure modular pipeline architecture (COMP-008)
Integrate embedding model (OpenAI API, local embedding service, or AWS Bedrock) with Haystack (COMP-003)
Configure Haystack to retrieve documents from Mayan EDMS; set up document chunking and preprocessing (COMP-002, COMP-003)
Index all OCR-extracted documents into vector database (COMP-003, COMP-008)
Integrate LLM provider (AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, or self-hosted) for RAG generation (COMP-003)
Implement RAG pipeline: query embedding → semantic search → context formatting → LLM inference
Configure pipeline monitoring: embedding latency, retrieval accuracy, LLM response time (COMP-007)

implementation_phases.name: REST API and Request Orchestration
activities: Develop custom REST API server (Node.js/Express or Python/FastAPI) (COMP-004)
Implement endpoints: POST /documents/upload, GET /documents/search, POST /documents/query, GET /documents/{id}, GET /api/health
Integrate FortifyAuth-API for JWT validation and RBAC enforcement on all endpoints (COMP-005)
Wire REST API to GdoczAI OCR, Mayan EDMS storage, and Haystack RAG (COMP-001, COMP-002, COMP-003)
Implement request validation, multipart file upload handling, and error response formatting
Deploy REST API on ECS behind Application Load Balancer with TLS/SSL termination (COMP-008, COMP-006)
Configure request logging and latency metrics export to OpenObserve (COMP-007)

implementation_phases.name: Observability, Monitoring, and Compliance
activities: Configure structured logging for all services: REST API, OCR, storage, authentication, RAG orchestration (COMP-007)
Create OpenObserve dashboards: API SLIs (latency, error rate, throughput), OCR metrics, RAG pipeline performance, authentication events
Set up alerts for: API error rate >5%, authentication failures, certificate expiration, database connection failures, OCR quality degradation
Export audit trails from Mayan EDMS and FortifyAuth-API to OpenObserve for compliance tracking (COMP-002, COMP-005, COMP-007)
Document data access for compliance: who accessed what document, when, and for what purpose
Implement trace instrumentation for RAG queries: track query flow from API → embedding → retrieval → LLM inference

implementation_phases.name: Security Hardening and Production Readiness

Implement API rate limiting per user/API key; protect against token exhaustion
Configure network security: restrict inter-service communication via security groups; deny public access except to ALB
Enable VPC Flow Logs for network traffic monitoring; export to OpenObserve (COMP-007)
Conduct penetration testing of authentication and authorization layer (COMP-005)
Verify encryption at rest (Mayan EDMS) and in transit (TLS/SSL on all connections) (COMP-002, COMP-006)
Test certificate rotation and renewal procedures; ensure zero-downtime renewal
Implement backup and recovery procedures; test restore procedures

Security testing: validate token validation, RBAC enforcement, TLS/SSL enforcement, encryption
Stress testing: identify failure modes under high load; test service recovery after failures
User acceptance testing: gather feedback on API usability, search quality, RAG answer accuracy
Performance tuning: optimize embedding model latency, LLM inference time, database query performance
Documentation: API specifications, deployment runbooks, troubleshooting guides, security hardening checklist
Production launch: enable monitoring alerts, on-call rotation, incident response procedures

findings: Modular microservices design with clear separation of concerns (OCR → Storage → Retrieval → API → Auth) is coherent and aligns with stated architecture style
Component responsibilities are well-defined; each component has clear inputs, outputs, and integration points documented

Architectural contradiction identified: COMP-006 (Transport Encryption) is marked as BUILD, but it is treated as a cross-cutting concern applied uniformly to all components rather than a discrete component with implementation artifacts. This conflates infrastructure configuration with a buildable component. TLS/SSL enforcement should either be: (a) removed as a standalone component and folded into COMP-004 REST API and COMP-008 AWS deployment, or (b) treated as a library/configuration pattern, not a component requiring independent build and deployment
Data flow explicitly defines end-to-end journey from document upload through OCR, storage, indexing, retrieval, and RAG generation. Flow is traceable and testable
Integration points (10 total) cover critical paths: REST API ↔ OCR, OCR ↔ Storage, Storage ↔ RAG, RAG ↔ API, API ↔ Auth, etc. No obvious missing integrations between core components
Risk of multi-service coordination complexity acknowledged but mitigation strategies (circuit breakers, error handling) not architecturally specified in blueprint; deferred to implementation phase

Assumption of LLM provider availability (AWS Bedrock or external) is explicit but integration with COMP-008 AWS orchestration layer is vague; unclear whether LLM is provisioned as AWS service or external call from deployed Haystack instance

Nine sequential data flows documented covering primary workflows: document upload, OCR processing, storage, embedding, semantic search, RAG query, and monitoring. Flows are logically ordered and traceable
Critical data flow verified: User query → Authentication → Embedding → Vector search → Document retrieval → LLM inference → Answer generation. This end-to-end path is architecturally sound

Data confidentiality preserved: Encryption in transit (TLS/SSL, COMP-006) specified on all flows; encryption at rest (Mayan EDMS, COMP-002) specified for storage layer. No plaintext data transmission identified in documented flows

Flow gap identified: No explicit data flow for error handling or retry logic. Document shows GdoczAI error handling is implemented (Phase 3, activity 3) but data flow for failed OCR → retry queue → downstream processing is not diagrammed. Implementation completeness risk

Flow gap identified: Embedding update/refresh workflow not documented. Initial indexing is clear (Phase 4), but workflow for re-indexing after document updates, deletions, or embedding model changes is absent. Vector DB consistency risk
Authentication token flow clear: FortifyAuth-API → JWT → REST API validation → RBAC checks → downstream service calls. Token refresh and expiration handling assumed but not explicitly diagrammed
Observability flow redundant but appropriate: All services → OpenObserve. Acceptable to have centralized logging; no data duplication or conflicting flows identified

Data flow does not specify serialization formats between components. Example: GdoczAI outputs 'structured JSON' (COMP-001 decision notes) but exact schema not documented. Mayan EDMS storage format unknown (database vs file-based). Vector embeddings format (dense vectors, sparse, or hybrid) unspecified. Integration risk without formal data contracts
10 integration points explicitly defined with source, target, and purpose. Each point maps to specific components (COMP-001 through COMP-008)
REST API (COMP-004) acts as central orchestration hub; all external requests flow through this component. Architectural pattern is consistent with microservices best practices

Critical integration: GdoczAI (COMP-001) → Mayan EDMS (COMP-002). Purpose stated as 'store OCR-extracted text and original document.' Implementation detail missing: Does GdoczAI write directly to Mayan EDMS API? Via message queue? Via file upload? Protocol unspecified. Risk: coupling assumptions may be violated

Critical integration: Mayan EDMS (COMP-002) ↔ Haystack (COMP-003). Purpose stated as 'retrieve documents for semantic indexing' and 'provide document chunks for RAG retrieval.' Bidirectional flow implied but integration pattern unclear. Does Haystack poll Mayan EDMS? Subscribe to change events? Batch fetch on schedule? Implementation gap

Authentication integration: FortifyAuth-API (COMP-005) validates tokens for REST API (COMP-004) and checks permissions with Mayan EDMS (COMP-002). Stated as 'sync RBAC roles and document permissions' but synchronization protocol not specified. Is it real-time? Cached? Risks: permission drift, eventual consistency issues

All services → OpenObserve (COMP-007) integration stated but no specification of log transport protocol, schema, or batching strategy. Implementation assumes all services have OpenObserve client libraries available. Compatibility risk if component languages/runtimes differ

AWS Cloud Integration (COMP-008) described as 'central orchestration' but integration with other components is infrastructure-level (provisioning, networking) rather than application-level API calls. Inconsistent abstraction: other integrations are data/control flows; COMP-008 integration is deployment topology

Integration with external LLM (AWS Bedrock, OpenAI) stated only in assumptions section and Phase 4 activities. No explicit integration point defined between Haystack (COMP-003) and LLM provider. Risk: responsibility ambiguous (Does Haystack integrate? Does COMP-004 REST API? Does COMP-008 orchestration?)

Encryption (COMP-006) integration stated as 'applied at REST API entry point' and 'downstream service connections.' No explicit integration points defined for how individual services enforce TLS/SSL. Risk: configuration details deferred to implementation; potential for misconfiguration

Integration testing plan mentioned (Phase 8) but no integration specification document (e.g., API contracts, message schemas, error handling agreements) defined in blueprint. Implementation gap for teams

Eight implementation phases defined with granular activities (62 total activities across all phases). Coverage is comprehensive for deployment lifecycle: foundation → security → storage → ingestion → retrieval → API → observability → testing

Phase 1 (Foundation and Security Infrastructure) specifies concrete deliverables: AWS VPC, RDS instances, FortifyAuth-API deployment, TLS/SSL setup, OpenObserve deployment, Secrets Manager. Actionable

Phase 2 (Data Storage Layer) specifies Mayan EDMS deployment, encryption configuration, vector database provisioning. Actionable but does not specify backup strategy or disaster recovery runbooks; assumes Phase 8 testing will validate

Phase 3 (OCR Pipeline) specifies containerization of GdoczAI, deployment on ECS, ingestion workflow, error handling, and monitoring. Adequate but does not specify OCR confidence thresholds, rejection criteria, or escalation for low-quality documents

Phase 4 (RAG Orchestration) specifies Haystack deployment, embedding model integration, document indexing, and RAG pipeline configuration. Incomplete: no specification of chunk size, overlap, context window limits for LLM integration; no specification of retrieval ranking strategy (BM25 vs semantic vs hybrid)

Phase 5 (REST API Development) specifies endpoint design, authentication integration, and orchestration wiring. Incomplete: no specification of request/response schema, error codes, pagination for large result sets, or API versioning strategy. Dependencies on COMP-004 BUILD decision are not validated

Phase 6 (Observability) specifies OpenObserve dashboard setup and alerting. Incomplete: no SLO/SLI definitions, no log retention policy specification, no audit trail schema definition for compliance. Assumes audit requirements are known (mentioned in risks but not in requirements)

Phase 7 (Security Hardening) specifies general security audit activities but lacks concrete hardening checks: WAF rules, rate limiting thresholds, DDoS mitigation strategy, RBAC test cases. Risk: security hardening deferred to execution without detailed specification

Phase 8 (Testing and Validation) specifies high-level test categories (integration, load, security, UAT) but no test specifications, acceptance criteria, or coverage targets defined. Example: 'Load testing: simulate concurrent users' — how many? For how long? What latency target?

Implementation notes in decision records (for COMP-001, COMP-002, COMP-003, COMP-005) provide detailed guidance but are scattered across decisions rather than consolidated in blueprint. Developers must cross-reference multiple sections

No specification of deployment infrastructure-as-code templates (Terraform/CloudFormation). Phase 1 assumes 'provision AWS' but actual IaC definitions not provided. Implementation gap: teams will spend time creating boilerplate that should be templated
No specification of CI/CD pipeline configuration. Phase 1 mentions 'Configure CI/CD pipeline' but no stages, build scripts, deployment triggers, or rollback procedures defined. Implementation gap

No capacity planning or resource sizing. Phases assume resource availability but no guidance on compute instance types, database size, vector DB capacity, or auto-scaling policies. Example: Phase 8 'load testing' will identify bottlenecks after deployment

No specification of data migration strategy for legacy documents or batch import. Assumed all documents ingested via REST API upload; no bulk import or integration with existing document repositories specified

Thirteen risks explicitly documented covering CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW severity categories. Coverage includes licensing, security, scalability, integration, operational, and architectural risks

CRITICAL risks properly identified: (1) Unknown licenses for major components (GdoczAI, Mayan EDMS, FortifyAuth-API) — mitigation is legal review; (2) No security audits — mitigation is independent assessment; (3) Custom REST API security — mitigation is code review and testing. Mitigations are explicit and actionable

Risk not identified: Dependency chain failure. Example: If Haystack (REUSE, COMP-003) relies on an unmaintained library or has an unpatched security vulnerability, the entire RAG pipeline fails. Transitive dependency risk not acknowledged. Recommendation: add continuous dependency scanning to Phase 7 or Phase 8

Risk not identified: LLM provider outage. If AWS Bedrock or OpenAI is unavailable, RAG queries fail. No fallback LLM provider or graceful degradation specified. Blueprint assumes LLM availability. Recommendation: specify fallback strategy (local model, alternative provider, or queued processing)

Risk not identified: Vector database corruption or inconsistency. If embeddings become stale after document updates or index is corrupted, semantic search accuracy degrades silently. No consistency checking or reindexing strategy specified. Recommendation: add periodic re-indexing validation and consistency checks

Risk not identified: Data export and compliance. GDPR requires ability to export user data. CCPA requires data deletion. No data export/deletion workflow specified in architecture. Blueprint assumes audit logging but not data subject access requests. Recommendation: add GDPR/CCPA compliance considerations to Phase 7

Risk not identified: Multi-tenancy isolation (if future requirement). Current architecture assumes single tenant (enterprise account). If multi-tenancy required, RBAC model must enforce data isolation at storage and retrieval layers. Recommendation: clarify single-tenant assumption or design isolation upfront

Scalability risk partially addressed. HIGH risk acknowledged for GdoczAI OCR throughput, but no scalability risk identified for: (1) Haystack semantic search latency under large vector DB size (millions of embeddings), (2) LLM inference latency as query volume increases, (3) Mayan EDMS storage scalability with large document volumes. Recommendation: expand scalability risk analysis

Operational risk partially addressed. MEDIUM risk acknowledged for certificate management, but no risk identified for: (1) Database backup and recovery procedures, (2) Vector DB disaster recovery, (3) Service dependency chain (if Mayan EDMS is down, entire system stops). Recommendation: add operational resilience risks

Cost risk not identified. AWS services (Bedrock, OpenSearch, RDS, ECS) incur non-trivial costs, especially for LLM inference and vector DB storage. No cost optimization or budget monitoring strategy specified. Recommendation: add cost monitoring and optimization as operational concern

Vendor lock-in risk not identified. Architecture relies on AWS services (Bedrock, OpenSearch, Certificate Manager, Secrets Manager). Switching providers is expensive. If team decides to migrate to GCP or Azure, significant rework required. Recommendation: identify cloud-agnostic vs AWS-specific components and consider hybrid approach

Third-party library maintainability risk partially addressed. Decisions note 'recent maintenance' as positive signal, but no specification of maintenance monitoring. If GdoczAI, Haystack, or FortifyAuth-API repositories become inactive (no commits for 1 year), fork/maintenance burden arises. Recommendation: add monitoring of library maintenance status to Phase 6 or Phase 7

Integration test risk not identified. Blueprint specifies end-to-end integration testing in Phase 8, but no risk identified if components have incompatible versions or API breaking changes. Example: Haystack version upgrade may require vector DB schema migration. Recommendation: add integration compatibility testing before production deployment

Data schema evolution risk not identified. As system evolves, OCR output schema may change, embedding model may upgrade (changing vector dimensions), or storage schema may require migration. No versioning strategy specified. Recommendation: add data versioning and schema migration plan

recommendations: CRITICAL: Resolve COMP-006 (Transport Encryption) abstraction issue. TLS/SSL is a cross-cutting infrastructure concern, not a discrete component with implementation artifacts. Recommendation: (1) Remove COMP-006 as standalone component, (2) Fold TLS/SSL configuration into COMP-004 (REST API) as HTTPS listener configuration and into COMP-008 (AWS deployment) as ALB and security group policies, (3) Add TLS/SSL configuration requirements to each component's implementation notes (e.g., service-to-service mTLS, certificate pinning). This eliminates the BUILD decision for a non-buildable concern

CRITICAL: Verify and document all third-party component licenses immediately. Conduct formal legal review of GdoczAI, Mayan EDMS, Haystack, FortifyAuth-API, and OpenObserve licensing terms. If any component uses GPL or AGPL, evaluate sublicense obligations. If incompatible with organizational policy, identify alternatives or plan for license exceptions before development begins

CRITICAL: Plan independent security assessments for major components before production deployment. Risk documentation acknowledges 'no security audit evidence.' Recommendation: (1) For REUSE components (Haystack, FortifyAuth-API, OpenObserve), obtain vendor security audit or conduct third-party assessment. (2) For ADAPT components (GdoczAI, Mayan EDMS), conduct focused security code review and penetration testing. (3) For BUILD components (REST API, TLS/SSL, AWS orchestration), implement secure development lifecycle (threat modeling, code review, SAST scanning, dynamic testing). Target: complete security assessment before Phase 8 launch

HIGH: Formalize data contracts between components. Define and document: (1) GdoczAI OCR output JSON schema (field names, data types, confidence scores), (2) Mayan EDMS document metadata schema and storage format, (3) Embedding vector format and dimensions, (4) REST API request/response schemas with examples. Recommendation: create OpenAPI 3.0 specification for REST API (COMP-004) and JSON Schema documents for internal data flows. Validate schemas during Phase 5 implementation

HIGH: Specify integration protocols between COMP-002 (Mayan EDMS) and COMP-003 (Haystack). Document: (1) How does Haystack discover and retrieve documents from Mayan EDMS? (Direct API call? Message queue? Batch ETL?), (2) What document fields are indexed for semantic search? (Title, content, metadata?), (3) How are document updates (edits, deletions) synchronized to vector index? (Real-time? Eventual consistency?). Recommendation: design integration specification during Phase 3 and validate during Phase 8 integration testing

HIGH: Define scalability and performance targets upfront. Establish acceptance criteria: (1) OCR processing latency: maximum X minutes per document, (2) Semantic search latency: maximum Y seconds for P95 tail latency, (3) RAG query end-to-end latency: maximum Z seconds, (4) Document indexing rate: X documents per hour. Recommendation: conduct capacity planning exercise during Phase 1 and validate assumptions during Phase 8 load testing. Define auto-scaling policies based on targets

HIGH: Specify LLM provider integration architecture explicitly. Risk documentation notes integration with 'AWS Bedrock or external LLM' but architecture is ambiguous. Recommendation: (1) Decision required: Is LLM called directly by Haystack (COMP-003)? By REST API (COMP-004)? By separate LLM gateway service? (2) Define API contract: How are prompts formatted? How many tokens allowed? What error handling for rate limits or unavailability? (3) Plan fallback strategy: What happens if LLM is unavailable? Queue requests? Degrade to simpler retrieval without generation?

MEDIUM: Create infrastructure-as-code templates for AWS deployment (COMP-008). Blueprint assumes 'provision AWS' but no Terraform/CloudFormation templates provided. Recommendation: (1) Create modular IaC templates for each Phase 1-2 component (VPC, RDS, vector DB, ECS cluster, ALB, Secrets Manager), (2) Include configuration parameters (instance types, database size, auto-scaling policies) as variables, (3) Add documentation for customization and environment setup. This accelerates Phase 1 execution and ensures reproducible deployments

MEDIUM: Define observability metrics and SLO/SLI targets. Phase 6 specifies OpenObserve dashboard setup but no specific metrics or targets defined. Recommendation: (1) Define Service Level Indicators: API P95 latency (target: <500ms), error rate (target: <0.1%), OCR success rate (target: >95%), embedding latency (target: <1s), RAG generation latency (target: <10s), (2) Define Service Level Objectives: API availability 99.5%, RAG answer accuracy >80% (via user feedback), (3) Create dashboards and alerts for each SLI. Use Phase 8 load testing to establish baseline metrics

MEDIUM: Plan data governance and compliance strategy. Blueprint mentions audit logging for COMP-007 but does not specify: (1) Data retention policy (how long to keep documents, logs, audit trails?), (2) Data deletion workflow (GDPR right to be forgotten), (3) Data export capability (GDPR data subject access requests), (4) Compliance certifications required (SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA?). Recommendation: conduct compliance assessment and add data governance requirements to Phase 7 (Security Hardening)

MEDIUM: Specify CI/CD pipeline configuration and deployment strategy. Phase 1 mentions 'Configure CI/CD pipeline' but no details provided. Recommendation: (1) Define build stages: syntax check, unit tests, integration tests, SAST scanning, container image build, registry push, (2) Define deployment stages: dev → staging → production, (3) Define rollback strategy: canary deployments? Blue-green? Feature flags?, (4) Define deployment frequency and SLA (e.g., release every sprint, 4-hour RTO). Document in IaC templates or separate CI/CD pipeline-as-code

MEDIUM: Add transitive dependency management and vulnerability scanning to implementation plan. Risk documentation does not address supply chain security. Recommendation: (1) Add continuous dependency scanning tool (e.g., Snyk, Dependabot) to CI/CD pipeline, (2) Pin all third-party library versions to prevent unexpected upgrades, (3) Establish policy for dependency updates (e.g., patch updates automatic, minor versions require approval, major versions require security review), (4) Add this to Phase 6 (Observability) or Phase 7 (Security Hardening)

MEDIUM: Specify RBAC model and permission matrix. FortifyAuth-API (COMP-005) is integrated but no explicit RBAC model defined. Recommendation: (1) Define roles: admin, document-uploader, searcher, query-generator, audit-viewer, (2) Define permissions per role: Who can upload? Who can search? Who can generate RAG answers? Who can view audit logs?, (3) Define document-level permissions: read, write, delete, share, (4) Document role-to-permission mapping and validate that FortifyAuth-API and Mayan EDMS models are aligned. Test RBAC enforcement during Phase 8

LOW: Clarify single-tenant vs multi-tenant architecture assumption. Blueprint assumes single-tenant enterprise deployment but does not explicitly state this. If future multi-tenancy is planned, data isolation at storage and retrieval layers requires architectural changes. Recommendation: document assumption and clarify if multi-tenancy is in scope for Phase 1 or deferred

LOW: Specify testing criteria and acceptance gates for Phase 8 (Testing and Validation). Blueprint lists test categories but no acceptance criteria. Recommendation: (1) End-to-end integration test: successful document upload → OCR → indexing → search → RAG generation (minimum 5 test cases covering happy path and error scenarios), (2) Load test: 100 concurrent users, 1000 documents in index, P95 search latency <500ms, error rate <0.1%, (3) Security test: validate JWT validation, RBAC enforcement, TLS/SSL enforcement, input sanitization (minimum 10 test cases per category), (4) UAT: 90% of user acceptance criteria met, no blocking issues. Define gate criteria before Phase 8 execution

LOW: Add documentation and knowledge transfer plan. Blueprint is comprehensive but implementation requires significant domain expertise (RAG, embeddings, vector DB, AWS services). Recommendation: (1) Assign documentation owner during Phase 5 (REST API development), (2) Create architecture diagrams (C4 model: Context, Container, Component, Code levels), (3) Document API specifications (OpenAPI), database schemas (ERD), data flows (sequence diagrams), (4) Create deployment runbooks and troubleshooting guides, (5) Plan knowledge transfer sessions with operations and support teams before Phase 8 launch

REUSE is justified by necessity—no better-evaluated alternative exists for purpose-built vector storage—but significant due diligence is required before deployment.

Radix Primitives is selected as the foundational UI component library for building COMP-006 (web interface). The evaluation confirms it explicitly provides 'accessible design system primitives and web app components,' directly matching the requirement to build responsive interfaces for support agents and customers. Accessibility-first design is particularly valuable for enterprise support systems requiring WCAG compliance. Radix is framework-agnostic (works with React and other frameworks), providing architectural flexibility. However, project health metrics, licensing, and security information are completely absent from evaluation evidence. REUSE is justified by Radix's established industry adoption, accessibility focus, and framework flexibility, but immediate verification of license and security posture is required.

data_flow: User submits support query via web UI (COMP-006) → KrakenD API Gateway (COMP-005) → OpenAM validation (COMP-004) → haystack RAG orchestration (COMP-002)
haystack embeds query → tidepool vector search (COMP-003) → retrieves k-nearest neighbor documents
haystack aggregates retrieved documents → invokes LLM with context → generates answer with source citations
Answer returned through KrakenD (COMP-005) → rendered in web UI (COMP-006)
Support documents ingested via COMP-001 → normalized and chunked → passed to haystack (COMP-002) → embeddings generated → stored in tidepool (COMP-003)
All services emit observability signals (logs, metrics, traces) → openobserve (COMP-008) → indexed and aggregated
Monitoring dashboard queries openobserve (COMP-008) → visualizes system health, API latency, LLM performance, retrieval quality
Third-party systems invoke REST APIs via KrakenD (COMP-005) → authenticate with OpenAM (COMP-004) → access search/RAG/ticket management endpoints
cubecos (COMP-007) orchestrates deployment and scaling of all containerized components across Kubernetes cluster

implementation_phases.name: Foundation & Security Verification
activities: Conduct immediate licensing and security due diligence on all REUSE components: verify haystack (Apache 2.0/MIT), tidepool (license unknown), OpenAM (CDDL or commercial), KrakenD-integration (license/parity with official KrakenD), Radix Primitives (MIT), cubecos (license), openobserve (license). Check CVE databases and security advisories for each.
Establish security baseline: threat modeling for RAG platform, identify attack vectors (prompt injection, document poisoning, unauthorized access), plan mitigation strategies.
Verify component project health: GitHub activity, contributor diversity, issue resolution SLA, maintenance roadmap for each reused component.
Set up development environment with Kubernetes cluster (local Kind or managed cloud cluster) for cubecos integration testing.
Create project scaffolding: repository structure, CI/CD pipeline skeleton, Docker containerization templates, Helm charts for Kubernetes deployment.

implementation_phases.name: Core RAG Infrastructure Setup
activities: Deploy and configure tidepool vector database: establish cloud storage backend (S3/GCS/Azure Blob), set up vector index schema, configure similarity search parameters.

Integrate haystack framework: set up RAG pipeline structure, configure document chunking strategies, select and integrate LLM backend (OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source), test end-to-end embedding and retrieval flow.

Implement COMP-001 (custom document ingestion service): build file upload handler, multi-format parser (PDF, DOCX, markdown), document chunking logic, metadata extraction. Integrate with haystack pipeline.
Test RAG pipeline with sample documents: verify embedding quality, semantic search accuracy, LLM answer generation latency, groundedness of generated answers.
Set up local development RAG testing environment with mock documents.

implementation_phases.name: Authentication & API Infrastructure
activities: Deploy and configure OpenAM: set up user repository (LDAP/database), configure authentication policies (password, MFA methods), define roles/permissions for support agents/customers/admins.
Deploy and configure KrakenD API gateway: set up service discovery, define route patterns for RAG endpoints, authentication middleware integration with OpenAM, request/response transformation rules.
Implement API endpoint contracts: design REST/GraphQL schemas for search queries, answer generation, ticket management, third-party integrations. Document OpenAPI/GraphQL specifications.
Integrate KrakenD with haystack RAG backend: configure service aggregation, test request routing, validate end-to-end API call flow.
Set up API rate limiting, versioning, and deprecation strategy.
Test authentication flow: login, token generation, API access with valid/invalid credentials.

implementation_phases.name: Frontend & User Interface
activities: Set up React/Vue/Angular frontend project with Radix Primitives component library.
Design and implement support agent interface: search UI with query input, results display with source citations, ticket management panels (create, view, update), knowledge base browser.
Design and implement customer self-service interface: simplified search UI, FAQ browser, ticket tracking dashboard, feedback mechanism.
Implement authentication integration: login redirects to OpenAM, session token management, logout/session expiration handling.
Connect frontend to KrakenD API gateway: implement search queries, answer display, ticket operations, real-time notifications.
Conduct accessibility audit: WCAG 2.1 compliance testing, screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation, color contrast validation.
Performance optimization: code splitting, lazy loading, asset compression.

implementation_phases.name: Observability & Monitoring Setup
activities: Deploy openobserve: configure log collection, metrics aggregation, trace sampling, storage backend for long-term retention.
Instrument all services with OpenTelemetry agents: emit logs from ingestion (COMP-001), RAG (COMP-002), vector store (COMP-003), API gateway (COMP-005), web UI (COMP-006).
Define LLM-specific metrics: token usage, latency percentiles, cost tracking, answer quality (groundedness, relevance), retrieval metrics (precision, recall).

Create observability dashboards: system health (CPU, memory, network), API performance (latency, throughput, error rates), RAG metrics (retrieval quality, LLM latency, hallucination rates), business KPIs.
Set up alerting rules: service down, error rate threshold, API latency SLA breach, vector search degradation, LLM token quota alerts.
Test observability pipeline end-to-end: generate synthetic load, verify metrics flow, validate dashboards.

implementation_phases.name: Cloud Infrastructure & Containerization
activities: Containerize all components: create Dockerfiles for ingestion service (COMP-001), haystack RAG service (COMP-002), API gateway (COMP-005), web UI (COMP-006), OpenAM, auxiliary services.
Deploy cubecos Kubernetes orchestration: provision managed Kubernetes cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS), configure network policies, storage classes for persistent volumes.
Create Helm charts for each service: deployment manifests, service definitions, config maps, secrets, resource requests/limits.
Configure auto-scaling policies: horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA) based on CPU/memory, request latency, custom metrics from openobserve.
Set up load balancing: ingress controller configuration, SSL/TLS termination, traffic distribution across service replicas.
Implement deployment pipelines: CI/CD integration (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), automated image builds, staging/production promotion gates.
Test Kubernetes deployment and scaling: manual scale tests, failure injection (pod restart), rolling updates.

implementation_phases.name: Integration & End-to-End Testing
activities: Test complete user journeys: customer searches support docs → RAG retrieves context → LLM generates answer → answer displayed in UI.
Test support agent workflows: upload new documents → ingestion processes → embeddings indexed → search finds new docs → answer incorporates new knowledge.
Test third-party API integrations: external system calls REST API → authenticates with OpenAM → retrieves answers programmatically → integrates into external ticketing system.
Conduct security testing: prompt injection attempts against RAG, unauthorized API access attempts, authentication bypass attempts, data exfiltration scenarios.
Load testing: simulate concurrent users, sustained high-volume queries, measure system performance under stress, identify bottlenecks.
Integration testing with mock LLM backends: validate RAG pipeline with multiple LLM providers, test fallback strategies for LLM failures.
Document integration points, test coverage matrix, known limitations.

implementation_phases.name: Production Hardening & Deployment
activities: Security hardening: enable network policies, implement pod security standards, configure RBAC, set up secret management (Vault/AWS Secrets Manager), enable audit logging.
Disaster recovery planning: backup strategies for tidepool vector store, OpenAM user repository, document metadata. Test recovery procedures.
Performance tuning: optimize vector search latency, haystack RAG pipeline performance, API gateway throughput, database query optimization.
Capacity planning: estimate resource requirements (CPU, memory, storage) based on load testing, set up monitoring for capacity utilization trends.
Documentation: architecture diagrams, deployment runbooks, operational procedures, troubleshooting guides, API documentation, administrator manual.
Staged rollout: deploy to staging environment, conduct full regression testing, gather feedback from internal users, fix issues, deploy to production with canary/blue-green strategy.
Post-deployment monitoring: validate all metrics flowing to openobserve, set up on-call alerting, establish incident response procedures.

implementation_phases.name: Optimization & Feedback Loop
activities: Monitor production performance: analyze openobserve dashboards for bottlenecks, latency hotspots, error patterns.
Collect user feedback: support agent usability, customer satisfaction, API integration feedback from partners.
Optimize RAG quality: analyze retrieved documents for relevance, analyze generated answers for accuracy, tune chunking strategies and embedding models if needed.
Optimize LLM cost: analyze token usage per query, explore model cost-benefit tradeoffs, implement caching for common queries.
Scale optimization: analyze auto-scaling behavior, adjust HPA thresholds, optimize resource requests/limits based on observed utilization.
Continuous security monitoring: track CVEs for all dependencies, apply patches promptly, conduct periodic security audits.
Feature roadmap: prioritize based on usage patterns, user feedback, performance metrics, plan incremental improvements.

findings: Architecture follows clear modular microservices pattern with well-defined responsibility boundaries across 8 components. RAG pipeline orchestration (COMP-002 → COMP-003) is logically coherent.
Component layering is consistent: ingestion → RAG orchestration → storage → API exposure → frontend. Data flow aligns with architectural intent.

CRITICAL CONTRADICTION IDENTIFIED: COMP-001 (custom BUILD) integrates to COMP-002 (haystack REUSE), but haystack is described as 'production-ready framework requiring integration with other components' (implementation note). Architectural tension exists: is haystack a plug-and-play RAG solution or does it require extensive custom integration? If former, building custom ingestion may be unnecessary (haystack may include ingestion). If latter, BUILD decision for COMP-001 alone is insufficient; haystack integration effort underestimated.

Security layer (COMP-004 OpenAM) is positioned post-API gateway in decision logic, but authorization is described as enforced 'on API endpoints and platform features.' No evidence that OpenAM integrates bidirectionally with backend services (haystack, vector store) for request-level access control. Potential architectural gap: does haystack enforce per-request authorization, or only API gateway level?

Frontend (COMP-006 Radix Primitives) is described as 'UI primitives, not complete component library,' yet no explicit mention of state management layer, API client library, or session management. Architectural component for client-side orchestration (Redux/Zustand/Context) not represented in blueprint.

Cloud infrastructure (COMP-007 cubecos) positioned as deployment orchestrator, but COMP-004 (OpenAM) deployment model unclear: is it containerized as Kubernetes service, or separate identity provider? If separate, integration responsibility between OpenAM and cubecos undefined.

Observability instrumentation (COMP-008 openobserve) described as receiving telemetry from 'all services,' but integration pathway for legacy/external components (third-party LLM APIs, external vector storage) not specified. Potential blind spots in observability.

API gateway (COMP-005 KrakenD-integration) is single point of routing for all external traffic, but no circuit breaker, failover, or service mesh patterns described. Single-point-of-failure risk not mitigated at architectural level.

Data flow shows LLM invocation via haystack, but LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, local) is abstracted away. If LLM provider changes or fails, architectural impact unclear (cold-start caching strategy, fallback LLM selection, cost implications).

Vector storage (COMP-003 tidepool) integration depth with haystack not detailed: does haystack abstract vector store API (pluggable backend), or is tidepool tight coupling? If latter, switching vector stores in future requires haystack re-architecture.

Primary data flow (search query → RAG → answer) is logically consistent and documented in 9 numbered flows. Bidirectional relationships clearly mapped (e.g., haystack retrieves from tidepool, stores results).

Ingestion data flow (COMP-001 → COMP-002 → COMP-003) is coherent: documents ingested, chunked, embedded, stored in vector index. Metadata propagation assumed but not explicitly detailed (does COMP-001 preserve document source/timestamp through COMP-002 to COMP-003?).

CRITICAL FLOW GAP: Third-party integrations flow (flow #7) shows API call to KrakenD then access to 'search/RAG/ticket management endpoints,' but ticket management backend not represented in component diagram. Where does ticket data originate? How does it flow through architecture? Ticket CRUD operations not mapped to specific components.

Authentication flow shows token validation at API gateway (COMP-005) and optional user context propagation to haystack (COMP-002), but revocation/session invalidation flow not documented. If user permissions change mid-session, is stale context used by haystack?

Observability data flow shows 'all services emit signals to openobserve,' but sampling strategy for traces not specified. High-volume systems (millions of queries/day) may require trace sampling; budget impact on openobserve storage not quantified.
Backup/disaster recovery data flow not documented: how are tidepool embeddings backed up? How are vector indices reconstructed if node fails? Backup intervals, retention policies not specified.
LLM cost tracking flow implied (observability metrics) but not explicit: does each haystack query emit LLM token count? How is cost aggregated and reported? Integration with billing system not shown.
Real-time collaboration flow (if support agents work on same ticket) not addressed in data flows. Session state synchronization, conflict resolution not documented.
Document update flow (user reuploads FAQ with corrections) not fully specified: does haystack re-embed only changed chunks, or full re-embedding? Vector index versioning strategy not described.
Frontend state management flow not represented: how does web UI (COMP-006) cache search results? Does it implement optimistic updates? Stale-while-revalidate patterns not documented.
Error recovery flows missing: if RAG fails to generate answer (LLM timeout, context truncation), what fallback is shown to user? Graceful degradation logic not mapped.
Component integration matrix (12 integration points documented) is mostly coherent, but several critical integrations lack implementation specificity.

CRITICAL INTEGRATION GAP: KrakenD (COMP-005) to haystack (COMP-002) integration marked as 'route search and RAG queries,' but protocol/interface undefined. Is haystack exposed as HTTP service, gRPC, direct Python import? If HTTP, who implements the REST wrapper? Implementation notes state 'implement REST API wrapper around haystack pipelines'—is this a KrakenD middleware or separate service?

OpenAM (COMP-004) to haystack (COMP-002) integration marked 'provide user context and permission scopes,' but access control enforcement undefined. Does haystack check permissions for each document retrieval? This has performance implications (N+1 auth checks). Integration pathway not detailed.
tidepool (COMP-003) to S3/GCS backup integration mentioned in COMP-007 implementation notes but NOT in integration matrix. Missing formal integration definition.

Web UI (COMP-006) to OpenAM (COMP-004) integration described as 'redirect users to login,' but OAuth2/OIDC flow not detailed. Silent refresh token rotation for session extension not specified. Integration complexity likely underestimated for production SSO.

Third-party integration with external ticketing systems mentioned (flow #7, implementation phase 7) but no specific integration pattern defined. API webhook pattern? Poll-based? Message queue? Integration paradigm choice deferred.

COMP-001 (custom ingestion) to haystack integration not specified in integration matrix, only in responsibility column. Missing formal integration definition. Does ingestion service directly call haystack APIs, or does it stage data for async processing?

OpenAM to cubecos (COMP-007) deployment integration: if OpenAM containerized in Kubernetes, how are persistent storage (user repository, configuration) managed? If OpenAM is external service, how is network routing secured? Integration strategy not specified.

haystack to external LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic) integration assumed but not documented in integration matrix. LLM provider selection, API key management (secrets rotation), provider failover not addressed.
COMP-003 (tidepool) blob storage backend integration (S3/GCS) mentioned in risks but not in formal integration matrix. Storage provider selection, access control, cost implications not documented.

Frontend (COMP-006) to openobserve (COMP-008) integration for client-side analytics mentioned in phase 4 but integration pattern not specified. Web analytics library (GA, Amplitude, custom)? OpenTelemetry JS SDK? Integration pathway undefined.

API versioning and backward compatibility between KrakenD (COMP-005) and clients mentioned in phase 3 but integration mechanics not specified. How are API versions routed? Deprecated endpoint sunset strategy?

Nine-phase implementation roadmap is comprehensive and covers major workstreams: foundation, RAG setup, auth/API, frontend, observability, infrastructure, integration testing, production hardening, optimization. Phases are logically sequenced and interdependencies mostly clear.

Phase 1 (Foundation & Security) appropriately prioritizes licensing/security due diligence given significant risk profile (7 REUSE components with unknown licenses/CVE status). Critical gate before proceeding.

CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION GAP: No explicit phase for 'Vector Search Quality Evaluation.' RAG architecture quality directly depends on embedding model selection, chunking strategy, and retrieval accuracy. Blueprint mentions 'test RAG with sample documents' in phase 2 but lacks structured quality metrics, tuning iteration, domain-specific evaluation framework. Retrieval quality not treated as first-class implementation concern.

CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION GAP: LLM Fallback and Cost Management not addressed in any phase. What happens when OpenAI API fails? Are cached responses served? Is local fallback LLM deployed? Token quota overflow handling not specified. Cost monitoring and optimization (phase 9) deferred too late; should be concurrent with RAG implementation.

Phase 2 (Core RAG Infrastructure) mentions 'select and integrate LLM backend' but vendor selection criteria not provided. Latency requirements (user-facing query: target <2s?), cost budget, model capabilities trade-offs not framed. LLM selection risk deferred.

COMP-001 (Document Ingestion) implementation in phase 2 is underspecified. 'Build file upload handler, multi-format parser, chunking logic' assumes trivial scope; production multi-format parsing (PDF extraction, table handling, OCR for images) is non-trivial. Implementation complexity likely underestimated.

Phase 3 lacks explicit API contract definition milestone. REST/GraphQL schema design should precede gateway/backend integration to prevent rework. OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification generation not mentioned.

Phase 4 (Frontend) lacks accessibility testing metrics. WCAG 2.1 compliance mentioned but testing methodology not specified. Manual audit vs. automated tools? VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) generation? Compliance evidence collection not planned.

Phase 5 (Observability) defers LLM-specific metrics instrumentation to 'define metrics' activity without specifying retrieval accuracy metrics (precision@k, recall@k, MRR), hallucination detection, or groundedness scoring. RAG quality observability architecture underspecified.

Phase 6 (Kubernetes) assumes 'all components containerizable' but COMP-004 (OpenAM) containerization strategy not detailed. OpenAM traditionally deployed on Java application servers; Kubernetes-native deployment requires careful design (stateful sets, persistent volumes for LDAP data).

Phase 7 (Integration Testing) lists user journey tests but lacks negative test scenarios: expired credentials, concurrent search/document-upload conflicts, vector store unavailability, LLM token exhaustion. Failure mode testing incomplete.

Phase 8 (Production Hardening) mentions 'canary/blue-green strategy' but traffic routing mechanism not specified. Who controls canary traffic split? Rollback criteria? Monitoring gates? Deployment orchestration underspecified.
Phase 9 (Optimization) is vague: 'analyze openobserve dashboards' lacks specific KPIs, SLA targets, or optimization decision frameworks. Feedback loop execution criteria not defined.
NO EXPLICIT PHASE FOR VENDOR LOCK-IN MITIGATION: If tidepool project abandoned, vector migration cost high. Phase for 'vector database abstraction layer' or migration tooling not planned.

NO EXPLICIT PHASE FOR SECURITY INCIDENT RESPONSE: Security testing in phase 7 is validation, not preparation. Incident response playbooks, security contact escalation, vulnerability disclosure process not planned.
Load testing mentioned in phase 7 but target metrics not specified. Concurrent user targets? Query throughput SLA? Vector search latency percentiles? Test environment sizing not defined.
Risk registry includes 20 identified risks spanning licensing, security, project maintenance, integration, scalability, and operational concerns. Breadth of risk coverage is good.

CRITICAL RISK UNDERSPECIFIED: 'Prompt Injection Security' listed as risk but mitigation strategy not proposed in architecture. No input validation layer, context isolation, or output sanitization described. Risk acknowledged but architectural response missing.

CRITICAL RISK UNDERSPECIFIED: 'LLM Failure Modes' (cascading unavailability, token quota exhaustion, degraded performance) identified in risks but no fallback mechanism designed into architecture. Circuit breaker pattern, cached responses, graceful degradation not documented.

CRITICAL RISK UNDERSPECIFIED: 'Build Component Complexity' for COMP-001 (custom ingestion) identified but mitigation not proposed. Should scope be reduced? Should third-party ingestion framework (Airbyte, Logstash) be evaluated despite not being in candidate pool? Risk acknowledged but architectural response missing.
License and security risks for all 7 REUSE components correctly identified as critical, with clear gate (Phase 1 verification) established. Mitigation approach appropriate.

Project maintenance risks for tidepool, OpenAM, KrakenD-integration, cubecos appropriately flagged, but no architectural fallback position specified. If cubecos abandoned, what is backup cloud deployment strategy? Risk identified without contingency plan.

GraphQL support gap (KrakenD-integration) correctly identified as integration risk. Mitigation (additional gateway, Apollo Server) mentioned in integration consistency findings but not in formal risk response.

Auto-scaling configuration risk for cubecos identified but mitigation strategy not specified. Should architecture include explicit Kubernetes HPA manifests in IaC templates? Risk identified without design mitigations.

Vector search quality risk (embedding model, chunking strategy, domain specificity) identified in risks but no evaluation methodology proposed. How will 'poor RAG output' be measured? What is acceptance threshold (e.g., 80% retrieval accuracy)? Risk identified without acceptance criteria.
Kubernetes operational complexity risk appropriately flagged with learning curve assumption (~2-3 weeks). Mitigation (team training, managed Kubernetes option like EKS) not explicitly planned.

NO RISK FOR COST UNPREDICTABILITY: LLM token costs potentially volatile (query complexity varies, model pricing changes). Vector storage costs (tidepool blob storage) potentially unknown. Budget overrun risk not explicitly listed.

NO RISK FOR DATA PRIVACY/RETENTION: If documents contain PII (customer names, email addresses in FAQs), how is data governed? GDPR right-to-forget, data residency not addressed. Privacy risk not captured.

NO RISK FOR VENDOR LOCK-IN (haystack): If haystack project stalls, migration to alternative RAG framework (LlamaIndex, LangChain) requires significant rework. Switching cost high. Vendor lock-in risk not captured.

NO RISK FOR MONITORING BLIND SPOTS: If openobserve fails or becomes unavailable, system operates blind. No fallback observability destination, no local logging fallback. Observability system failure risk not captured.

NO RISK FOR DOCUMENT POISONING: If documents uploaded to COMP-001 contain adversarial examples designed to manipulate RAG output, how is this detected? No content filtering, anomaly detection described. Security risk gap.

ASSUMPTION-RISK LINKAGE INCOMPLETE: 9 assumptions listed but not linked to corresponding risks. E.g., 'Radix Primitives framework assumption' is linked to risk of 'development scope underestimation,' but this relationship not explicit in risk statement.

Risks for COMP-002 (haystack) integration, COMP-003 (tidepool) scalability, and COMP-005 (KrakenD GraphQL) appropriately flagged with 'Risk of requiring additional custom development.' Estimated effort (weeks? months?) not quantified.
Risk timeline: Phase 1 gates critical licensing/security risks, but implementation-phase risks (schema design, API contract definition) not gated. Late-stage discovery of integration issues possible.

recommendations: URGENT: Resolve licensing and security due diligence immediately before architecture commitment. Create explicit go/no-go gates for Phase 1 completion: all 7 REUSE components must have confirmed license (Apache 2.0, MIT, CDDL, etc.), no critical CVEs at deployment time, and active maintenance verified (GitHub activity within past 3 months). If tidepool, cubecos, or KrakenD-integration fail gates, evaluate alternatives or reconsider REUSE decision before proceeding.

CRITICAL: Add explicit 'Vector Search Quality Evaluation' phase between Phase 2 and Phase 3. Define acceptance metrics for RAG quality: retrieval accuracy (precision@k, recall@k for domain-specific test set), relevance of top-k results (human scoring or proxy metrics), latency percentiles (p50, p99), cost per query. Establish tuning iteration loop for embedding model, chunking strategy, and retrieval parameters. Quality gates must be passed before API and UI implementation.

CRITICAL: Design and document LLM fallback architecture before RAG implementation. Define failure modes: LLM API timeout (fallback to cached response + user notification), token quota exhaustion (reject request gracefully), provider outage (fall back to alternative model if available, or enable FAQ-only mode). Implement circuit breaker pattern in haystack wrapper. Document cost guardrails and quota monitoring thresholds.

CRITICAL: Clarify haystack integration model and COMP-001 scope boundary. Determine if haystack includes document ingestion/parsing capabilities (it may have built-in PDF/text parsers). If yes, reevaluate COMP-001 BUILD decision—custom ingestion may be limited to format-specific parsing (e.g., proprietary FAQ XML structure). If no, confirm COMP-001 scope includes all format handling. Document haystack integration pathway explicitly (Python SDK vs. REST wrapper).

URGENT: Add explicit 'API Schema Design & Contract' phase before Phase 3 gateway/backend integration. Define REST endpoints (GET /search?query=..., POST /rag, etc.) and GraphQL schema upfront. Generate OpenAPI 3.0 spec and GraphQL SDL as contract. Review with frontend team (COMP-006) and third-party integrators before implementation. Prevents downstream rework and integration delays.

URGENT: Clarify KrakenD-integration repository status and feature parity before committing. Verify: (a) Is this official KrakenD-maintained wrapper or community project? (b) Does it support GraphQL natively or via middleware? (c) Is JWT validation middleware included? (d) What is maintenance SLA? If community project, evaluate official KrakenD instead or use simpler API gateway (Tyk, Kong) with better GraphQL support.

URGENT: Design and document access control architecture for COMP-002 (haystack) integration with COMP-004 (OpenAM). Define: (a) Do users have document-level permissions (can agent see all FAQs or subset)? (b) Does haystack filter retrieved documents by user permissions? (c) What is performance impact (document-level filtering may require post-retrieval filtering, not pre-retrieval). (d) How is permission context passed from KrakenD to haystack? Include authorization filter in haystack pipeline or API gateway layer?

URGENT: Establish production LLM provider selection criteria before RAG implementation. Define tradeoffs: OpenAI (high quality, high cost, no data residency control), Anthropic (high quality, high cost), open-source (Llama, Mistral via self-hosted or API, lower cost). Specify latency requirement (<2s for user-facing queries?), cost budget, model size constraints. Design haystack LLM provider abstraction to enable future provider switching without code changes.

HIGH PRIORITY: Add explicit 'Vector Database Abstraction Layer' to architecture. If tidepool adoption is forced by REUSE decision, implement thin abstraction interface so alternative vector stores (Weaviate, Milvus, Pinecone) can be swapped if tidepool project stalls. Design: Define vector store interface (embed, search, delete), implement tidepool backend, document interface for future backends. Mitigates vendor lock-in risk.

HIGH PRIORITY: Add 'Content Filtering and Adversarial Document Detection' to Phase 1 security planning. Define: (a) Input validation rules for uploaded documents (max size, allowed formats, malware scanning). (b) Anomaly detection for adversarial examples (e.g., documents with contradictory statements, injection-pattern text). (c) Output filtering for LLM responses (detect prompt injection echoes, PII leakage). Integrate with COMP-008 monitoring for anomaly alerting.

HIGH PRIORITY: Expand Phase 4 (Frontend) to include explicit 'State Management Architecture' design. Define: (a) Client-side state management library (Redux, Zustand, Context API). (b) API caching strategy (React Query, SWR, Apollo Client). (c) Session and authentication token management (refresh token rotation, logout). (d) Optimistic updates for search results. Include as architectural component or update COMP-006 description to clarify scope.

HIGH PRIORITY: Add 'Data Retention and Compliance' phase to implementation roadmap. Define: (a) Document data retention policy (how long are uploaded FAQs stored?). (b) User data retention (search history, ticket data, user profiles). (c) GDPR right-to-forget implementation (how to delete embeddings for specific documents from tidepool?). (d) Audit log retention for compliance (OpenAM events, API access logs). (e) PII handling in documents (should customer names be redacted before embedding?). This should be Phase 1 or Phase 2 gate.

HIGH PRIORITY: Clarify cubecos deployment model for stateful components. Document: (a) Is OpenAM containerized in Kubernetes or external identity provider? (b) How is tidepool blob storage provisioned (local PVC, cloud object storage)? (c) How are persistent volumes backed up and recovered? (d) What is Kubernetes networking model (service mesh, ingress controller)? Include Helm chart templates in Phase 6.

HIGH PRIORITY: Add 'Incident Response and Disaster Recovery' to Phase 1 planning. Define: (a) RTO/RPO targets (recovery time/data loss objectives). (b) Backup/restore procedures for vector database, OpenAM user repository, application state. (c) Incident response playbook (who to notify, escalation procedures, rollback authority). (d) Failover strategy (does multi-zone deployment exist?). (e) Testing schedule (quarterly DR drill?). Document before Phase 6 production hardening.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Reassess COMP-001 (custom ingestion) scope and complexity. Multi-format parsing (PDF, DOCX, markdown, CSV) is non-trivial. Evaluate: (a) Can existing libraries (PyPDF, python-docx, apache-tika) reduce custom code? (b) Should chunking strategy be domain-specific (preserve code blocks, table structures) or generic? (c) Is OCR required for scanned documents or only digital PDFs? Document scope clearly to avoid underestimation.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Define 'Observability Instrumentation Standards' before Phase 5 implementation. Specify: (a) Which OpenTelemetry signals to emit (logs, metrics, traces)? (b) Sampling rates for traces (100% in dev, X% in prod?). (c) Log levels and retention (DEBUG for dev, ERROR for prod?). (d) Metrics cardinality limits (prevent explosion of metric combinations). (e) Custom metrics for RAG quality (retrieval accuracy, hallucination rate, cost per query). Create instrumentation checklist for each component.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Establish 'Load Testing and SLA Definition' before Phase 7 integration testing. Define targets: (a) Concurrent users / queries per second target. (b) Latency SLA (p50, p95, p99 for search query response). (c) Error rate threshold (0.1%?). (d) Vector search latency limit (must be <500ms?). (e) LLM generation latency limit (<1.5s?). Create load test scenarios (concurrent users, sustained high volume, burst traffic). Benchmark in Phase 7, use results to right-size infrastructure in Phase 6.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Plan 'Security Testing and Penetration Testing' as explicit Phase 8 activity. Define scope: (a) Prompt injection attacks on RAG (craft malicious documents/queries). (b) Authentication bypass attempts (JWT tampering, session fixation). (c) Unauthorized API access (missing permission checks). (d) Data exfiltration (information disclosure via error messages). (e) Denial of service (vector search overload, LLM token exhaustion). Schedule professional penetration test post-Phase 8.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Document 'Third-Party Integration Protocol' in Phase 3 API design. Define: (a) Supported integration patterns (webhook callbacks, REST polling, message queues). (b) API authentication for third parties (API key, OAuth2 client credentials). (c) Rate limiting and quota per third-party client. (d) Sandbox/staging environment availability. (e) SLA guarantees and support model. Create integration partner onboarding guide.

MEDIUM PRIORITY: Add 'Cost Monitoring and Budget Controls' as concurrent activity during Phase 2-3. Track: (a) LLM token costs per query (integrate with LLM provider metering).
